_comment: KT2 comparison job: Chatterbox on the same fragment Kokoro read, plus FLUX.1-schnell on the imagined shots NASA has no footage of.
tts_sentences: Imagine at nine o'clock tomorrow morning, the Moon stops holding its orbit.
Not an explosion. Not a collision. It simply begins to fall.
For the first week, you would barely notice.
The Moon looks a little larger each night, the way a car in your mirror looks closer without seeming to move.
Tides are a tug of war, and the Moon is winning harder every hour.
By day nineteen, it is twice its normal size in the sky, and high tide is climbing six meters above the old line.
Coastal cities are not flooded yet.
They are simply wet, twice a day, a little deeper each time.
And here is the part almost nobody expects.
The Moon never actually reaches the ground.
Something tears it apart long before that, and what happens next lasts a million years.
